cases.expect: Inverse derivation uses the declared pairing.

cases.input: A published dependency type is refined and re-released in a later registry release.
cases.expect: The type retains its dependencyTypeId, gains a new typeVersion, and edges pinned to the prior typeVersion continue to resolve to the prior semantics.

cases.input: A dependency type is declared solely as an element of RegistryRelease.typeDefinitions with no dependencyTypeId of its own.
cases.expect: The declaration is rejected because per-type supersession and deprecation cannot be expressed.

cases.input: A RegistryRelease carries status 'effective' with no declared status enumeration and no published-to-effective transition rule.
cases.expect: The release is rejected until status enumerations and transition rules are declared at registry, release and type level.

cases.input: A type declares directionality 'directed' and inverseOfTypeRef pointing at its converse term.
cases.expect: Inverse assertions are derivable on demand and a stored converse edge is detectable as a duplicate.

cases.input: Canonical and converse edges are stored as independent facts using two type terms with no declared inverse pairing or symmetry flag.
cases.expect: The duplication rule is unenforceable and the registry state is rejected until an inverse pairing is declared.

cases.input: A single dependency edge is asserted with three endpoints under a type declaring arity 3.
cases.expect: The edge is rejected as invalid, not recorded as low-confidence.

cases.input: A dependent requires one prerequisite and either of two alternatives.
cases.expect: A PrerequisiteGroup with groupSemantics 'all' containing a nested 'any' group is recorded, with every member expressed as a binary edge.

cases.input: An interface type and a package type are declared composition-eligible with a recorded basis.
cases.expect: A TypeCompositionRule for the ordered pair is published and multi-hop paths across the two types compose.

cases.input: A co-location relation is registered as a dependency type with a canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction.
cases.expect: The registration is rejected; co-location requires relationClass 'adjacency', which carries no canonical direction.

cases.input: A propagation profile is published with typeFilter, phaseWindow, traversalDirection, depthLimit, lagBound, unknownEdgePolicy, stopConditions and evidenceThreshold.
cases.expect: An immutable versioned PropagationProfile release is created and is pinnable by reference.

cases.input: not-assessed and unresolved are mapped onto unknown in the registry state vocabulary.
cases.expect: The mapping is rejected; all five states remain distinct and unresolved carries its own definition.

cases.input: A consumer holding registry release n must discover release n+1 using only supersedesRelease, which is recorded on n+1.
cases.expect: The discovery path is rejected as structurally impossible; a ReleaseSupersession link record is required.

cases.input: A type declaring lag is published with lagCalendarRef, ianaZone and tzdbRelease.
cases.expect: The lag semantics are resolvable and reproducible across evaluations.

cases.input: A type declares a lag duration with no calendar, zone or timezone database release.
cases.expect: The type is rejected; the lag invariant is unenforceable without a pinned time basis.

cases.input: A registry release records validFrom, validTo and retiredAt.
cases.expect: Each timestamp declares its time axis and zone, and event, observation and ingestion times remain distinct.

cases.input: The registry references WM-XCT-037 with purpose 'Dependency edge and impact semantics'.
cases.expect: The purpose string is rejected; impact semantics belong to Impact Scenario and must not be re-asserted inside the edge work item.

cases.input: A dependency-type vocabulary declares references to a risk record, an observation and a citation while excluding ownership of all three and consuming none.
cases.expect: The references are rejected as unjustified coupling introduced to satisfy a reference-count minimum.
